title: The Central Limit Theorem for Sums
short: A sum of n independent copies of X is close to normal, with mean nμ and standard deviation σ√n.
trouble: Students use σn or σ/√n for the spread of a sum. For a sum it is σ√n; σ/√n belongs to the average.

blocks.html: The law of large numbers says an average settles near its mean. The central limit theorem says more: the shape of a sum of many independent pieces is close to a normal curve, whatever the pieces look like. In the sampling distribution of a mean you used this for averages; here it is stated for sums.

If $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ are independent with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, then for large $n$ the sum $S_n = X_1 + \cdots + X_n$ is approximately normal with $$E[S_n] = n\mu, \qquad \operatorname{SD}(S_n) = \sigma\sqrt{n}, \qquad P(S_n \le s) \approx \Phi\left(\frac{s - n\mu}{\sigma\sqrt{n}}\right).$$

The mean and standard deviation of $S_n$ come from linearity and from adding the variances of independent terms ($n\sigma^{2}$). The normal shape is the deep part. A sketch with moment generating functions: standardize, $Z_n = \frac{S_n - n\mu}{\sigma\sqrt{n}}$. Its MGF is the product of $n$ identical factors, each about $1 + \frac{t^{2}}{2n}$ for large $n$, so $M_{Z_n}(t) \approx \left(1 + \frac{t^{2}}{2n}\right)^{n} \to e^{t^{2}/2}$, the MGF of the standard normal.

blocks.name: prob-convolve
blocks.cap: The sum of several independent uniform numbers. Add copies: the shape quickly becomes a bell curve with mean n times one half and standard deviation growing like the square root of n. Switch to the average to see it narrow instead.

blocks.name: sampling
blocks.cap: Even from a skewed population, averages of samples pile up in a nearly normal shape.

blocks.title: Boxes on a pallet
blocks.q: Boxes weigh 500 g on average with standard deviation 10 g, independently. Find the approximate probability that 36 boxes weigh more than 18.1 kg in total. Use $\Phi(1.67) = 0.9525$.

blocks.title: Total call time
blocks.q: Calls last 5 minutes on average with standard deviation 3 minutes, independently. Find the approximate probability that 49 calls take more than 4 hours in total. Use $\Phi(0.24) = 0.5948$.

blocks.title: A total that is rarely exceeded
blocks.q: With the boxes above, find the weight that 36 boxes stay below about 95% of the time. Use $\Phi(1.645) \approx 0.95$.
steps: Two sums of the same pieces differ only in $n$: doubling the number of boxes doubles the mean but multiplies the spread by only $\sqrt{2}$.

blocks.html: Using $\sigma n$ or $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$ for the spread of a sum. For a sum it is $\sigma\sqrt{n}$; $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$ belongs to the average, $\frac{S_n}{n}$. Check: a sum of more pieces is more spread out, but not in proportion to $n$, because independent errors partly cancel.
